# Implement the client retry policy

The repository in `/app` holds `shipclient`, our HTTP client library. Engineering standards are published in the `docs` service, which you can use through the `docs` MCP server.

Implement `retry_delay` in `/app/shipclient/retry.py` so that it follows the current standards for retrying outbound HTTP requests: which failures and which requests are retried, how many attempts are made, how long to wait, and how `Retry-After` is handled, including the settings that differ per service. The docs service also holds superseded and draft versions of some standards; follow the ones in force.

Keep the function's signature and docstring contract, and use the Python standard library only. `/app/tests` has a few tests you can run with `cd /app && python -m unittest`; your implementation will also be checked against cases they do not cover.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

"""Retry policy for outbound HTTP calls made through shipclient."""

from datetime import datetime


def retry_delay(
    method: str,
    request_headers: dict[str, str],
    attempt: int,
    status: int | None,
    response_headers: dict[str, str],
    now: datetime,
) -> float | None:
    """Seconds to wait before the next attempt, or None to give up.

    `attempt` is the number of the attempt that just failed, 1 for the first.
    `status` is None when there was no response (a connection error).
    `now` is the current time, timezone-aware UTC.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError

import unittest
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from shipclient.retry import retry_delay

NOW = datetime(2026, 9, 16, 10, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


class RetryDelayTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_first_retry_of_a_get(self):
        self.assertEqual(retry_delay("GET", {}, 1, 503, {}, NOW), 0.25)

    def test_not_found_is_final(self):
        self.assertIsNone(retry_delay("GET", {}, 1, 404, {}, NOW))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

results.content: {"type": "text", "text": "{\"id\":\"http-client-standard-v3\",\"title\":\"HTTP client standard (v3)\",\"tags\":[\"api\",\"client\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-04\",\"body\":\"# HTTP client standard (v3)\\n\\nStatus: current. Adopted 2026-08-04. Supersedes v2 (http-client-standard-v2).\\n\\nThis standard applies to every outbound HTTP call made through our client libraries.\\n\\n## When to retry\\n\\nA failed request is retried only when both of these hold:\\n\\n1. The failure is retryable: a connection error (no response at all), or a response with status 429, 502, 503 or 504. No other status is retried. In particular 500 is not retried, because our services return 500 only for bugs that a retry will not fix.\\n2. The request is safe to repeat: see the idempotency rules (doc idempotency-rules).\\n\\n## How many times\\n\\nBy default a request is attempted at most 5 times in total, counting the first attempt. After the last allowed attempt fails, give up.\\n\\n## How long to wait\\n\\nThe wait before the next attempt is exponential: 0.25 s after the 1st attempt, then doubling (0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, ...), never more than the backoff cap, which is 8 s by default. The client library adds jitter in the transport layer; the delay function itself returns the exact value.\\n\\nFor 429 and 503 responses that carry a Retry-After header, see the rate limit rules (doc rate-limit-handling): they can make the wait longer, or stop the retries.\\n\\n## Retry profiles\\n\\nA request names the service it calls in the `X-Service` request header. A service can have a retry profile: a doc tagged `retry-profile` that sets three values for requests to that service: the attempt limit, the backoff cap, and the longest accepted Retry-After wait. These replace the defaults of this standard and of the rate limit rules. Everything else stays as stated here: which failures and which requests are retried, the 0.25 s first delay and the doubling.\\n\\nA service can have several profile docs (older revisions, proposals). Only a doc whose status line says it is current applies. A request without `X-Service`, or to a service that has no current profile, uses the defaults. Service names are matched exactly, ignoring case; header names are case-insensitive.\\n\"}"}

{"type": "text", "text": "{\"id\":\"rate-limit-handling\",\"title\":\"Rate limit handling\",\"tags\":[\"api\",\"client\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-04\",\"body\":\"# Rate limit handling\\n\\nStatus: current.\\n\\nApplies to responses with status 429 or 503 that carry a Retry-After header. Other statuses ignore Retry-After.\\n\\nRetry-After holds either a number of seconds (an integer) or an HTTP date. For a date, the wait is the number of seconds from now until that date, and a date in the past means a wait of 0.\\n\\nAn HTTP date has exactly this layout: `Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:00:05 GMT` (three-letter day name, comma, two-digit day, three-letter month name, four-digit year, 24-hour time, and the zone `GMT`). HTTP dates are always in GMT. A date with any other zone name or with a numeric offset is malformed, and so is a date in any other layout.\\n\\n- If the Retry-After wait is more than the longest accepted wait, 30 seconds unless the service's retry profile sets another value, do not retry at all.\\n- Otherwise wait whichever is longer: the Retry-After wait or the exponential delay from the HTTP client standard. The backoff cap does not apply to the Retry-After wait.\\n- A malformed Retry-After value is ignored, as if the header were absent.\\n\\nHeader names are case-insensitive.\\n\"}"}

steps.message:
I implemented `retry_delay` in `/app/shipclient/retry.py` following the current docs. The two existing tests pass. I didn't write further tests, so the other rules below are untested. I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status "success".

- **What is retried:** connection errors and statuses 429, 502, 503 and 504. 500 is not retried. POST and PATCH are retried only with a non-empty `Idempotency-Key` header. GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT and DELETE are always eligible.
- **Attempts and delay:** the default is 5 attempts in total. The wait is 0.25 s, doubling each time, capped at 8 s.
- **`Retry-After`:** it is read only for 429 and 503. It accepts an integer number of seconds or an HTTP date in the exact `Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:00:05 GMT` layout. A malformed value is ignored. A wait longer than the service's limit (30 s by default) means no retry. Otherwise the wait is the longer of `Retry-After` and the backoff, and the backoff cap doesn't apply to it.
- **Service settings:** the `X-Service` header picks the profile, matched case-insensitively. I used only the profiles marked current: catalog, ledger, auth, payments, ledger-export, reports, inventory, search, shipping and media. The draft profiles (notify, the newer shipping and payments ones), the superseded revisions and the withdrawn geo profile are ignored. Notify and geo therefore use the defaults.
- **Dates:** I don't check that the day name in an HTTP date matches the actual weekday. The docs only specify the layout, so a wrong weekday with a valid layout is accepted. Impossible dates like 31 Feb are treated as malformed.
